ref_clues.ref_content: The rx_break_err interrupt is triggered if a break condition has been detected. A break condition is defined as the RX pin being continuously low for more than a programmable number of character-times (via CTRL.RXBLVL, either 2, 4, 8, or 16). Only one interrupt is generated per break -- the line must return high for at least half a bit-time before an additional break interrupt is generated. The current break status can be read from STATUS.BREAK. If STATUS.BREAK is set but INTR_STATE.BREAK is clear then the line break is still going on but interrupt has been cleared. If STATUS.BREAK is clear but INTR_STATE.BREAK is set then there has been a line break for which software has not cleared the interrupt but the line is now back to normal. Frame errors will continue to be reported after a break error.

The rx_frame_err interrupt is triggered if the RX module receives the START bit (0) and data bits but did not detect the STOP bit (1). In a real frame error the stop bit will be present just at an incorrect time. The start of a line break matches a frame error with all data bits zero and one frame error interrupt will be raised. If the line stays zero until the break error occurs, the frame error will be set at every char-time. Frame errors will continue to be reported after a break error. The effects of the line being low for certain periods: <10 bit-times: Frame Err if STOP=0; 10 with parity: No; 10 no parity: Yes; 11 to RXBLVL*char: Yes; >RXBLVL*char: Frame error every char-time, break at RXBLVL.
